ch29-open.title: Follow the presenter
ch29-open.standfirst: Lock your viewport to someone else's, and keep their video in a floating window while you work — so the room can move together.

ch5-follow.heading: Lock your viewport to someone else's
steps: In the participant strip along the bottom, hover any tile that is not your own; the tooltip reads Click to follow their view.
Click the tile. Your viewport zooms and pans to match theirs and stays locked as they move around the canvas.
An 👁 eye badge appears on that person's tile to show you are following them; the tooltip now reads Following — click to stop.
Click the same tile again to stop following — or press <kbd>Esc</kbd> anywhere to release the lock instantly.
Following someone else, or having them leave, also ends the follow.
ch5-follow.outcome: While following, your canvas tracks the other person's visible region automatically — useful when someone is walking the room through a drawing.
ch5-follow.note: Clicking your own tile does not follow anything; it opens your profile editor (display name, company, avatar) instead. The tooltip for your tile reads Your profile.

host.html: Following is a personal, local action — you choose to follow, and only your view moves. No one can force you to follow them, and following someone never moves their view.

ch5-follow.figcap: A followed tile showing the 👁 eye badge.

ch4-floating.heading: The floating presenter window
steps: Open the Video layout popover and turn on Floating presenter (the row below the three surfaces).
A small picture-in-picture card appears over the canvas, showing the focused person's camera (or avatar) with their name.
Drag the card by its header to move it — on release it snaps to the nearest corner, and that corner is remembered.
Click Minimise to shrink it to a small circular puck; click the puck to bring the card back.
ch4-floating.outcome: You keep watching the presenter in a corner while the canvas stays fully usable. The window shows the same focused person every other surface agrees on.
ch4-floating.note: The floating window only ever shows someone else — never your own face — and it is hidden automatically in Gallery mode, where everyone is already full-screen. The minimise tooltip reads Reopen presenter window on the puck.
ch4-floating.figcap: The floating presenter PiP, snapped to a corner with Minimise and Hide controls.
